question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

The interior designer received a __________ from her client for choosing furniture that would perfectly __________ the walls and floors.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. compliment, complement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"compliment"** refers to a polite expression of praise or admiration. (प्रशंसा या तारीफ)
 
 
• **Example:** She received a compliment on her beautiful dress.
 
 
• The word **"complement"** refers to something that completes or goes well with something else. (पूरक)
 
 
• **Example:** The new curtains perfectly complement the color of the walls.
 
 
• In the given sentence, "compliment" and "complement" are the correct words because the designer received praise (compliment) for choosing furniture that perfectly matched or completed (complemented) the walls and floors.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. compliment, complement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: counsel, council**
 
 
• **"Counsel"** means advice or guidance, typically given formally. (सलाह)
 
• **Example:** She sought counsel from her mentor before making the decision.
 
• **"Council"** refers to an assembly or advisory group formed to discuss and decide on important matters. (परिषद)
 
• **Example:** The city council voted on the new zoning regulations.
 
• These words do not fit the context of the sentence, as the sentence refers to praise and matching, not advice or an assembly.
 
 

 
• **Option 2: complement, compliment**
 
 
• This option has the correct words but in the wrong order. The sentence requires "compliment" first and "complement" second to make sense in the given context.
 
 

 
• **Option 4: council, counsel**
 
 
• This option also uses "council" and "counsel," which refer to a group or advice, respectively. These do not suit the context of the sentence.
